### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, each of the ten activities A33, A34, A35, A37, A38, A39, A40, A41, A42 and A43 ran in only about half of the cases (roughly 48–53 in 100 traces, about once per case). In the later window, each of them runs in about 98–100 in 100 cases, still about once per case (recurrence stays near zero). [OCC001, OCC005, OCC006, OCC010, POS003, POS008]
- The ten activities formed two blocks that were mutually exclusive earlier: a pair such as A33 with A39 co-occurred in at most about 1–2 in 100 cases, each otherwise appearing without the other. In the later window, such cross-block pairs co-occur in about 96–98 in 100 cases, with the first-block activity (A33–A38) before the second-block activity (A39–A43) in about 96 in 100 of them. [REL025, REL029, REL033, REL040, REL051, REL055]
- Within each block, activities already co-occurred whenever their block ran (about 48–53 in 100 cases earlier) and now co-occur in about 98–100 in 100; in both windows both orders occur in similar shares, so the order inside each block stays unfixed. [REL021, REL030, REL045, REL056, REL060, REL065]
- A30 and A31 appear in all cases in both windows. In the later window, A30 precedes each of the ten activities in about 97–99 in 100 cases and A31 follows each of them in about 97–99 in 100; earlier, A30 preceded whichever single block ran, and A31 came after it (A31 co-occurred with the first block in about 48 in 100 cases and with the second in about 52 in 100). [REL001, REL006, REL010, REL011, REL016, REL020]
- Routing shifted accordingly: A30's outgoing transitions went earlier to both blocks (A34 about 15%, A42 about 13%, A41 about 11% of observed outgoing edges) and now go almost only to the first block (A38 about 24%, A37 about 21%, A34 about 20%, A33 about 19%, A35 about 15%), with A39–A43 near zero. Direct transitions from A33, A34, A35 and A37 into A31 (about 15–27% of their outgoing edges earlier) have essentially disappeared. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Relative event positions moved consistently: A30 earlier (mean about 0.64 to 0.55), first-block activities earlier (about 0.72–0.73 to 0.63), second-block activities later (about 0.72 to 0.76) and A31 slightly later (0.82 to 0.84). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS006, POS008, POS012]
- The seven lag items each rest on only 1–4 observations in one window (for example A30–A40 has 103 supporting cases earlier but 1 later), so they carry little weight. [LAG001, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which two activity groups that were alternative branches in the earlier window — {A33, A34, A35, A37, A38} and {A39, A40, A41, A42, A43} — are executed together in the later window, one after the other: A30, then the first group in mixed internal order, then the second group in mixed internal order, then A31. Earlier, each case ran exactly one of the two groups (about 48–53 in 100 cases each) with A31 last; in the later window essentially every case runs both groups. [REL025, REL033, REL051, OCC001, OCC006, DIR001, POS003, POS008]

This is supported directly and consistently: the alternatives-together change is shown relationally (cross-group co-occurrence rising from about 0–2 in 100 to about 96–98 in 100 with a stable first-before-second order), participation of all ten activities rose to near-universal, and the routing and position changes fit the same picture (A30 now leads only into the first group, and the first group's direct edges into A31 vanished, as expected once the second group sits between them). With 99 control-flow items qualifying against roughly 1.2 expected if nothing had changed, chance sampling cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [REL025, REL046, DIR001, DIR002, OCC001, POS001, POS008]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a change in routing logic from a shift in the case mix (for example, the later window containing only cases of the both-groups kind); positions are event positions, not clock times; and the lag items, with 1–4 observations in one window, were not load-bearing. [LAG001, LAG005, POS001]

Other differences: only minor remnants at noise level — a few new outgoing edges with about 0.5% shares (for example A30 to A08 and A30 to A10) and recurrence-support changes of at most about 1 in 100 cases. [DIR001, DIR002, OCC001, OCC003]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

We have two windows of 200 traces each. Screening: 241 units tested, 99 items qualified, 1.2 expected without change. That's a huge excess — 99 items vs 1.2 expected. So the count is many times larger than chance expectation. This means we're beyond "insufficient evidence" territory; the screening comparison passes decisively.

Now let me understand the behavioural pattern.

OCC items (CF_OCC): A33, A34, A35, A37, A38, A39, A40, A41, A42, A43 — all show trace participation rising from about 0.48–0.53 (roughly half of traces) to about 0.98–0.995 (nearly all traces). Mean occurrences per trace also roughly doubles from ~0.5 to ~1.0. So these ten activities went from being executed in about half the cases to being executed in nearly every case. Recurrence support stays near zero (each activity occurs once per trace).

DIR items: 
- DIR001 (source A30): before, outgoing transitions spread over A37, A42, A40, A34, A39, A41, A43, A35, A33, A31, A38, A48, A26 (with A42 highest at 0.129, A34 0.153). After: concentrated on A37 (0.205), A34 (0.2), A38 (0.24), A35 (0.15), A33 (0.19), with A40 nearly gone (0.005), A39/A41/A42/A43 gone. So A30 now leads to A33–A38 group rather than A39–A43 group.
- DIR002 (source A33): before, A31 was the biggest target (0.268), plus A38, A37, A35, A34. After: A31 gone (0), targets A38, A35, A34, A37, plus small shares to A39–A43. So A33 no longer leads to A31.
- DIR003 (source A34): before A31 0.155, A38 0.278, A37 0.237, A33 0.165, A35 0.144. After: A31 gone, A33 0.206, A35 0.19, A38 0.19, A37 0.196, plus small A39–A43.
- DIR004 (source A35): before A31 0.163, A33 0.276, A34 0.204, A37 0.184, A38 0.153. After: A31 nearly 0, A34 0.26, A33 0.20, A37 0.196, A38 0.12, plus small A39–A43.
- DIR005 (source A37): before A31 0.206, A35 0.268, A38 0.186, A33 0.175, A34 0.144. After: A31 0.005, A35 0.22, A38 0.21, A33 0.19, A34 0.175, plus small A39–A43.

So a consistent story: A31 was a common successor of A33, A34, A35, A37 (and appeared after A30 sometimes) in the before window; in the after window, transitions to A31 from these activities have essentially disappeared. Meanwhile A39–A43 were alternative successors of A30 before; after, A30 leads to A33–A38.

POS items:
- POS001 (A30): mean relative position decreased from 0.637 to 0.554 — A30 occurs earlier in traces in the after window.
- POS002 (A31): mean position increased slightly from 0.817 to 0.843.
- POS003–POS007 (A33, A34, A35, A37, A38): support rose from ~0.48 to ~0.995, and mean position decreased from ~0.72–0.73 to ~0.63. So these activities now occur in nearly all traces and earlier (relative position ~0.63 vs ~0.73).
- POS008–POS012 (A39–A43): support rose from ~0.52 to ~0.98, and mean position increased from ~0.72 to ~0.76. So A39–A43 now occur in nearly all traces and later.

REL items: many. Let me group:

REL001–REL010: pairs (A30, A33/A34/A35/A37/A38/A39/A40/A41/A42/A43). Before: cooccurrence ~0.48–0.53, A_only ~0.47–0.52 (A30 present, B absent). After: cooccurrence ~0.98–0.995, A_only ~0.005–0.02. And A_before_B ~0.97–0.995. So A30 and each of A33–A43 now co-occur in nearly all traces, with A30 before the other.

REL011–REL020: pairs (A31, A33...A43). Before: cooccurrence ~0.48–0.53, A_only (A31 only) ~0.47–0.52, B_before_A (A33 before A31) ~0.47–0.525. After: cooccurrence ~0.98–0.995, B_before_A ~0.97–0.99. So A31 now co-occurs with each of A33–A43 in nearly all traces, and A33–A43 come before A31.

REL021–REL024, REL030–REL032, REL038, REL039, REL045: pairs among A33, A34, A35, A37, A38 (and A37-A38). Before: cooccurrence ~0.48, neither ~0.51 (both absent together — they occurred in the same half of traces). After: cooccurrence ~0.995, neither ~0.005. Order mixed both before and after (A_before_B and B_before_A both substantial). So these pairs are executed without fixed order, but now co-occur in nearly all traces.

REL025–REL029: pairs (A33, A39/A40/A41/A42/A43). Before: cooccurrence ~0.005–0.015, A_only ~0.47–0.48, B_only ~0.515. After: cooccurrence ~0.975–0.98, A_before_B ~0.96. So A33 and A39–A43 were in disjoint sets of traces before (mutually exclusive alternatives), now co-occur in nearly all traces with A33 first.

REL033–REL037: pairs (A34, A39–A43): same pattern — before cooccurrence 0–0.01, after ~0.975 with A34 before.

REL040–REL044: pairs (A35, A39–A43): same pattern.

REL046–REL050: pairs (A37, A39–A43): same pattern.

REL051–REL055: pairs (A38, A39–A43): same pattern.

REL056–REL065: pairs among A39–A43 (A39-A40, A39-A41, A39-A42, A39-A43, A40-A41, A40-A42, A40-A43, A41-A42, A41-A43, A42-A43). Before: cooccurrence ~0.52, neither ~0.47. After: cooccurrence ~0.98, neither ~0.02. Order mixed both windows.

LAG items:
- LAG001 (A30→A40 within 5 steps): before, lags spread 1–5; after, only lag 1 but support after = 1 (only 1 observation!). Weak support.
- LAG002 (A30→A41): after support 1. Weak.
- LAG003 (A30→A43): after support 1. Weak.
- LAG004 (A34→A31): before support 95, after support 4. Weak after.
- LAG005 (A37→A39): before support 1, after support 121. Before weak.
- LAG006 (A37→A43): before support 1, after support 104. Before weak.
- LAG007 (A38→A31): before support 96, after support 4. Weak after.

LAG items have very low support in one window each, so they're weak evidence individually. But the REL and DIR and OCC items are strong.

Now the overall picture:

Before window: There appear to be two alternative branches. Roughly half the traces contain A33–A38 group (participation ~0.48–0.49), and roughly half contain A39–A43 group (participation ~0.52–0.53). A33–A38 co-occur with each other (cooccurrence ~0.48, neither ~0.51) and are mutually exclusive with A39–A43 (cooccurrence ~0–0.015). A30 precedes whichever group occurs (A30 participation is 1.0 in both windows; REL001–REL010 show A30 co-occurs with each of A33–A43 in after; before, cooccurrence ~0.48–0.53 equals the group's participation, A_only ~0.47–0.52 meaning A30 present without that activity in the other half). A31 comes after the A33–A38 group (B_before_A: A33 before A31 ~0.48) and A31 participation... wait, A31's participation isn't in OCC items. POS002 shows A31 support 1.0 in both windows. So A31 occurs in all traces in both windows. Before, A31 co-occurred with A33–A38 in ~0.48 of traces (when that branch ran) and was A_only in ~0.515 (when the A39–A43 branch ran). After, A31 co-occurs with everything.

After window: all of A33–A43 occur in nearly every trace (~0.98–0.995). A30 occurs before all of them (A_before_B ~0.97+). A31 occurs after A33–A43 (B_before_A ~0.97+). A33–A38 mutually unordered among themselves; A39–A43 mutually unordered among themselves; A33–A38 each before A39–A43 (A_before_B ~0.96+).

So the change: before, the process had two alternative blocks — one containing A33–A38 (followed by A31) and one containing A39–A43 — of which each case executed one. After, both blocks execute in every case: A30 → (A33–A38 in some order) → (A39–A43 in some order) → A31. Also A30's position moved earlier (POS001: 0.637 → 0.554), and A31's position slightly later (0.817 → 0.843), consistent with the process now containing more activities between A30 and A31.

Wait — is A31 after A39–A43 too? REL011–REL020 show A31 pairs with A33–A43: B_before_A means the second-listed activity (A33 etc.) before A31. For pairs (A31, A39) etc., B_before_A ~0.97 means A39 before A31. Yes, so A31 comes after both groups.

Also DIR002–DIR005: before, A33/A34/A35/A37 led to A31 with shares ~0.15–0.27; after, those transitions to A31 essentially vanish (A31 component ~0–0.005). That's consistent: A31 used to directly follow the A33–A38 block; now the A39–A43 block sits between them, so the direct edges A33→A31 etc. are gone (A31 now follows A39–A43 instead). DIR001: A30 before led to both groups (A34 0.153, A42 0.129, A39 0.094, A41 0.114, A43 0.099, A40 0.074, A37 0.079, A38 0.074, A33 0.074, A35 0.094...); after, A30 leads to A33–A38 (A38 0.24, A37 0.205, A34 0.2, A33 0.19, A35 0.15) and almost never directly to A39–A43 (A40 0.005). Consistent with A39–A43 now being reached via the A33–A38 block rather than directly from A30.

Hmm, but wait: is it that the two blocks became sequential, or that the second block became mandatory? Before, each trace had one of the two blocks. After, each trace has both. The participation of A39–A43 rose from ~0.52 to ~0.98; participation of A33–A38 rose from ~0.48 to ~0.995. So both blocks became mandatory (executed in essentially every trace), and they execute in sequence: A33–A38 block first, then A39–A43 block, then A31.

Alternatively: it could be described as a loop/parallel? The REL data shows A33 before A39 etc. consistently (A_before_B ~0.96), and within groups mixed order. So sequential blocks with internal unordered sets.

Now, how to characterise the hypothesis per the instructions:

The instruction about "a change in how often existing paths are taken" requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows, and only the shares between alternatives shift. Here, that's not the case in the simple sense: A33–A38 and A39–A43 were mutually exclusive alternatives before (cooccurrence ~0), and now co-occur in ~98% of traces. This is not a shift in path frequencies between alternatives; it's that two alternative branches became jointly executed — activities that were alternatives became sequential (REL guidance: "Activities that rarely or never occur in the same trace in one window but usually do in the other changed between being alternatives and being executed together."). That's a structural change: the exclusive-or between the two blocks became a conjunction (both blocks executed, in sequence).

So the main hypothesis: a structural change where two previously alternative activity groups (A33–A38 vs A39–A43) became executed together in sequence within the same case — i.e., the branch choice was removed and both blocks now run one after the other (A33–A38 first, then A39–A43), with A30 before both and A31 after both. Support: OCC (participation ~0.48→~0.99 for both groups), REL (mutually exclusive pairs A33×A39–A43 etc. went from cooccurrence ~0 to ~0.97 with consistent A33-before-A39 order; within-group pairs went from co-occurring in ~48% to ~99%), DIR (A30's outgoing shifted from both groups to only A33–A38; direct edges into A31 from A33–A38 disappeared), POS (A30 earlier, A31 later, group activities earlier/later consistent with insertion).

Could it be that a new activity was added? No, all activities were present in both windows with substantial support.
